debutant.intro: Setting foot on the sand for the first time? Welcome. Beach is not a by-product of indoor: it's a sport in its own right, with its own rules and its own culture. Here's the vital minimum so you don't sink.

sections.title: The 5 mistakes to avoid at all costs

items.title: 1. Trying to hit too hard
items.body: Placement >> power. A placed poke beats 10 spikes that fly out of bounds. The offensive philosophy of beach sums up in one line: "if your only tool is pounding the angle, you'll get blocked every time" (AVP).

items.title: 2. Receiving with finger sets
items.body: Almost always a fault in beach (hand set on 1st contact = double whistle). Absolute reflex: BUMP by default on anything that isn't hard-driven.

items.title: 3. Open-hand tip
items.body: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (rule 13.2.3 — fault). Must be replaced by a poke (middle knuckles) or a cobra (rigid extended fingertips).

items.title: 4. Neglecting communication
items.body: Talk on EVERY ball: "MINE!", "YOURS!", "FREE", "OUT". The 2011 Swiss Championships study shows +26 points of attack efficiency with calls vs without. Silence kills.

items.title: 5. Bad hydration / no sunscreen
items.body: Ruins a whole day. Water-resistant SPF 50+ (renew every 2 h), 1-2 L of water per session, electrolytes past 1 h, UV glasses, cap.

items.title: 3 touches max — block INCLUDED
items.body: THE major difference vs indoor. The block counts as the 1st of the 3 touches. After a touched block, only 2 touches remain to return the ball.

items.title: No open-hand tip
items.body: See mistake #3. Replace with poke or cobra.

items.title: Over-set perpendicular to the shoulders
items.body: If you send the ball over with a hand set, the trajectory MUST be strictly perpendicular to your shoulder line (straight forward or straight backward). Any oblique trajectory = fault.

items.title: No rotations
items.body: Free placement of both players on the court. No position fault.

items.title: 1 set to 21 (2-point gap), 3rd set to 15
items.body: Best of 3 sets. Tie-break to 15 if needed.

items.title: Side change every 7 points (5 in tie-break)
items.body: To balance sun and wind. Immediate change, no break.

sections.title: First reflex: the bump
sections.body: On sand, by default, you play EVERYTHING with the bump. It's the safest move, the one least called by the ref, and the best suited to imperfect positioning in the wind. The hand set on reception is reserved for high-level competition with a perfect ball.

sections.title: Choosing your partner
sections.body: Complementarity (tall blocker + fast defender), shared drive to improve, easy communication. In 2v2, the duo's mindset matters as much as technique.

items.title: ✓ Beach ball
items.body: Mikasa VLS300 or equivalent

items.title: ✓ Portable or club net
items.body: Height 2.43 m M / 2.24 m W

items.title: ✓ Hydration
items.body: 1.5 to 2 L of water per session, electrolytes

items.title: ✓ Sun protection
items.body: Water-resistant SPF 50+, cap, UV glasses

items.title: ✓ First aid kit
items.body: Aloe vera, band-aids, painkillers

items.title: ✓ Sand socks (optional in summer)
items.body: If sand > 45 °C

items.title: ✓ Carb snack
items.body: Banana, gel, energy bar

transition.intro: You've been playing indoor for years and want to switch to beach? Good news: your fundamentals come with you. Bad news: you'll have to unlearn three deeply ingrained reflexes. Here's the roadmap.

items.title: Touches
items.body: The block counts as the 1st touch. You can no longer chain block + dig + set + spike. After a touched block: 2 remaining touches max.

items.title: Strict finger setting
items.body: Refereeing far stricter than in the gym. Absolute hand synchronization. No body pivot. Over-set perpendicular to the shoulders.

items.title: No tip
items.body: The open-hand tip is FORBIDDEN. Mandatory replacement: poke or cobra.

items.title: Finger reception = fault
items.body: Except on hard-driven balls. Reflex: bump by default.

items.title: Sand surface
items.body: Movement 30% slower, jumps -5 to -15 cm, energy cost × 1.5 to × 2. Anticipation matters more than raw speed.

items.title: Total versatility
items.body: No more fixed position. You serve, receive, set, attack, block, defend. In turn, every rally.

items.title: Reduced roster
items.body: 2 players, no substitute. No libero.

items.title: 2v2 mindset
items.body: Total visibility between partners, constant communication, emotional management more exposed.

sections.title: What stays the same
sections.body: Your fundamental technical moves: bump, set, spike, serve. Your reading of the block and attacker. The importance of a clean contact. Line/angle, short/long concepts. Your indoor background is NOT lost — it just needs adjusting.

items.title: 1. The open-hand tip
items.body: Replace immediately with POKE (middle knuckles) or COBRA (rigid fingertips).

items.title: 2. The rotating set
items.body: Shoulders must stay perpendicular to the over-set trajectory. No body pivot.

items.title: 3. Systematic hand set on reception
items.body: BUMP by default. The hand set on reception is reserved for very settled sets and very clean players.

items.title: 1. The tomahawk
items.body: High defense for soft balls that your beach dig cannot legally play. Essential.

items.title: 2. The poke / cobra
items.body: Replaces your tip. Your #1 placement tool.

items.title: 3. Hand signals and 2v2 communication
items.body: Not optional. Before every serve from your side, the blocker signals behind the back. The defender adapts position.

items.title: W1-W2 — Adaptation
items.body: Stabilize the bump on sand, first serves, heat and hydration management.

items.title: W3-W4 — Beach tools
items.body: Poke and tomahawk, attacking with feet in the sand, managing the diminished jump.

items.title: W5-W6 — Tactics
items.body: Blocking at the net, block → defense transitions, hand signals.

items.title: W7-W8 — Competition
items.body: Complete tactics, first recreational tournaments, reading the opponent's play.

tournoi-loisir.intro: Running a recreational beach tournament is three things: choosing the right format for the number of teams, securing a compliant setup, and setting simplified rules everyone agrees on. The rest is logistics.

sections.title: Recommended formats by number of teams

items.title: 4 teams
items.body: Round robin + top 2 final. Duration ~2-3 h. Simplest format.

items.title: 6 teams
items.body: 2 pools of 3 + semi-finals + final. ~3-4 h.

items.title: 8 teams
items.body: 2 pools of 4 + crossover semis + final. ~4-5 h.

items.title: 12 teams
items.body: 3 pools of 4 + single elimination. Full day.

items.title: 16 teams
items.body: 4 pools of 4 + single elimination. Full day.

items.title: 24+ teams
items.body: Pools + main bracket + consolation bracket. Weekend.

items.title: Court
items.body: 16 × 8 m, free zone 3 m min (5-6 m at FIVB level). Sand depth 40 cm minimum.

items.title: Portable net
items.body: Height 2.43 m (M / mixed) or 2.24 m (W / recreational). 2.35 m for FFvolley mixed.

items.title: Lines
items.body: PVC tape + soft stakes. Width 5 cm.

items.title: Antennas
items.body: Optional in recreational, mandatory in competition.

sections.title: Simplified rules
sections.body: 1 set to 21 (or 15 for a quick format). No tie-break or "sudden death" at 25. Rotating serve. Self-refereeing. In doubt: replay. Beach spirit first — the sport is festive.

items.title: ✓ Balls
items.body: 1 per court + 2 spares

items.title: ✓ Nets and posts
items.body: Adjustable height by category

items.title: ✓ Lines + stakes
items.body: Contrasted PVC tape

items.title: ✓ Water jugs
items.body: Several liters per team per day

items.title: ✓ Scoreboards
items.body: At least one per court

items.title: ✓ First aid kit
items.body: Aloe vera, band-aids, painkillers, backup sunscreen

items.title: ✓ Tent / parasols
items.body: Shade zone for rest between matches

items.title: ✓ Sound system if > 12 teams
items.body: Announcements, vibe

items.title: ✓ Team list + schedule
items.body: Printed and posted

items.title: ✓ Prizes / trophies
items.body: Podium rewards

items.title: ✓ Recycling bins
items.body: Clean tournament, clean image

sections.title: Useful apps
sections.body: BeachUp (beachup.app, 16,500+ courts referenced worldwide) · Beach Volleyball App (App Store) · Tournaments by SportEasy · Toornament.com · CHAMP'S (champs.fr, streaming).

lecture-jeu.intro: Reading the opponent in beach is 50% of the defensive work. You have only 2 defenders to cover 16 × 8 m — the only way to hold is to anticipate. Here's the full method, from warm-up to stopping your feet before the hit.

sections.title: During warm-up (the crucial 5 min)
sections.intro: The 5 minutes of warm-up at the net are a scouting goldmine. Note mentally:

items.title: Who sets better?
items.body: One of the two will set more than the other. Identify who.

items.title: Who hits hard / who shoots?
items.body: The "hammer" and the "placer" reveal themselves fast.

items.title: "Line player" vs "angle player"
items.body: Natural tendency: the line or the diagonal.

items.title: Handedness
items.body: Righty / lefty. Affects attack angles.

items.title: Individual tics
items.body: One player who always looks at the target before hitting, another who loads low for the poke, etc.

sections.title: Cues to read before the hit (in order)

items.title: 1. Set quality
items.body: Tight to the net → open angles, hard hit likely. Off the net → closed angles, shots likely. Behind the attacker → poke very likely.

items.title: 2. Approach
items.body: Aggressive straight line → hard swing. Braked or shortened → shot or poke.

items.title: 3. Shoulders at the load
items.body: Aligned to the line → line. Open → angle / cross. Closed late → cut or tip.

items.title: 4. Arm and wrist
items.body: Straight extended → swing. Dropping elbow → cut or poke.

items.title: 5. Individual tendencies (scouting)
items.body: What you noted in warm-up and early in the match. Constant update.

items.title: Base position in the middle of the back
items.body: Neutral start at 1-1.5 m from the end line, centered.

items.title: Slide toward the zone on the set
items.body: As soon as the set quality is readable, slide to prepare the zone to cover.

items.title: Stop the feet BEFORE the attacker's contact
items.body: Golden rule — impossible to react if you're still moving.

items.title: Perfect first step
items.body: First impulse in the actual ball direction, never an approximation.

sections.title: In the match: constant adaptation
sections.body: Keep a mental mini-log (that player has hit 4 times on the line, 0 times on the diagonal). Adapt in real time. Provoke imbalance (short serve on the weak receiver to force them to play the 2nd touch). Re-read the wind on every side change (every 7 points in a normal set, 5 in the tie-break).

sections.title: Recommended drill
sections.body: "Five blind serves": your partner serves you into whichever zone they choose; you must call out loud what you read ("line", "angle", "cut", "short"…) BEFORE the ball arrives. Score out of 5. Target: 4/5 minimum after a few sessions.
